title: TaskHub Actions
description: Defines actions, tasks, and pipelines for the TaskHub extension.

id.description: Unique identifier for the action (e.g., button.build, pipeline.analyze).

title.description: The label displayed in the UI for this action.

type.description: Defines special item types like separators or folders.

children.description: If type is 'folder', this contains nested action items.

description.description: A short explanation shown in the UI for what this action does.

tasks.description: A list of one or more tasks to execute in sequence.

successMessage.description: A message to show when the entire task sequence (pipeline) completes successfully.

failMessage.description: A message to show if any task in the sequence fails.

id.description: Unique identifier for the task within the pipeline. Used to reference its output.

type.description: The type of the task to execute.

command.description: The command to execute. Can be a direct string or an OS-specific object. Required for 'shell' and 'command' types.

env.description: Environment variables to set for the task. Values support interpolation.

cwd.description: Current working directory for the command. Defaults to ${workspaceFolder}.

revealTerminal.description: Controls terminal visibility for 'shell' type tasks.

options.description: Options for 'fileDialog' or 'folderDialog' types, based on VS Code's OpenDialogOptions. Keys not listed here are passed through to VS Code unchanged.

canSelectMany.description: Allow picking several files (fileDialog) or folders (folderDialog). Everything picked is exposed as ${taskId.paths} (array of absolute paths), ${taskId.names} (array of base names) and ${taskId.count}. The single-value references (${taskId.path}, .dir, .name, ...) keep pointing at the first item. In an 'args' array, an element that is exactly "${taskId.paths}" expands into one argument per item; anywhere else the array is joined with spaces.

openLabel.description: Label of the confirmation button, e.g. "Select firmware".

defaultUri.description: Where the dialog opens, as a path or URI. When omitted TaskHub reopens the location this task last used.

filters.description: Extension filters, e.g. { "Firmware": ["elf", "bin", "hex"] }. Ignored by folderDialog.

canSelectFiles.description: Whether files can be picked. Leave unset: fileDialog already allows files, and folderDialog forces this to false.

canSelectFolders.description: Whether folders can be picked. Leave unset and use type 'folderDialog' instead, which forces this to true.

placeHolder.description: The placeholder text for 'inputBox' or 'quickPick' type.

password.description: If true, the input box will be masked (for 'inputBox' type).

prefix.description: Text to prepend to the user input (for 'inputBox' type). The final value will be: prefix + userInput + suffix

suffix.description: Text to append to the user input (for 'inputBox' type). The final value will be: prefix + userInput + suffix

validatePattern.description: For 'inputBox': a regex the user input must match. Non-matching text is rejected live with 'validateMessage'. An invalid pattern is ignored. e.g. '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\\d+$' for a Jira ticket key.

validateMessage.description: For 'inputBox': message shown when the value fails 'validatePattern'. Defaults to a generic 'invalid format' message.

extractPattern.description: For 'inputBox': a regex applied to the interpolated 'value' to derive the prefilled default. Uses capture group 1 if present, else the whole match; no match prefills empty. e.g. extract a Jira key from a branch name with '[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\\d+'.

oneOf.description: Array of simple string items for 'quickPick' type.

value.description: Value substituted for '${taskId.value}' when this item is picked. Defaults to the label. An array expands into several arguments in 'args' elements and 'command' tokens (e.g. ['--option','b']); an empty array adds no argument at all.

oneOf.description: Array of quick pick items with labels and optional descriptions.

items.description: List of items to select from (for 'quickPick' type).

canPickMany.description: If true, allows multiple selection (for 'quickPick' type). Results include 'value' (first selection), 'label' / 'labels', lossless 'labelList', 'values' (comma-separated), 'valueList' (array), and 'custom' (false for multi-select).

default.description: For 'quickPick': label to activate initially, or labels to preselect when canPickMany is true. Explicit default takes precedence over remembered selection. Supports variable interpolation.

allowCustom.description: For single-select 'quickPick': allow a non-empty value not present in items to be typed and returned directly. Cannot be combined with canPickMany.

rememberLastSelection.description: For 'quickPick': remember the selected label(s) and whether a single value was custom per workspace, action, and task, then restore them on the next normal run. An explicit default takes precedence. Selections derived from sensitive runtime context are not stored.

itemsFromCommand.description: For 'quickPick': a shell command whose stdout becomes the pick list (one item per non-empty, trimmed line). Runs in 'cwd' (or the workspace folder) via the login shell. Supports interpolation and the OS-specific object form. When set, 'items' is ignored. e.g. 'git for-each-ref --format=%(refname:short) refs/remotes/origin' to list origin branches.

itemsExclude.description: For 'quickPick' with 'itemsFromCommand': exact line(s) to drop from the command output (e.g. 'origin/HEAD'). Ignored when 'itemsFromCommand' is not set.

oneOf.description: An exact variable reference that resolves to an array, such as '${files.paths}' or '${pick.valueList}'.
A fixed list of values to iterate over. Entries support variable interpolation.

forEach.description: Run this non-interactive task once per item, sequentially. Inside the task use '${each}' or '${each.value}', plus '${each.index}' (0-based), '${each.number}' (1-based), and '${each.count}'. Dynamic lists are limited to 1000 items; accumulated results use the action result-size limit.

message.description: The confirmation message to display (for 'confirm' type). Supports variable interpolation.

confirmLabel.description: Label for the confirm button (for 'confirm' type). Defaults to 'Yes'.

cancelLabel.description: Label for the cancel button (for 'confirm' type). Defaults to 'No'.

oneOf.description: A direct path to the tool executable.
OS-specific paths for the tool executable.

tool.description: Path to the tool executable. Can be a direct string or an OS-specific object. Optional for 'zip' and 'unzip' types: if omitted, the built-in zip engine is used (.zip archives only). Specify a tool (e.g. 7z path) for other formats.

inputs.description: Specifies inputs from previous tasks' outputs. e.g., {'archive': 'zipTaskId', 'destination': 'folderDialogTaskId'}

file.description: Legacy alias for 'archive'. References a previous task that provides an archive path.

archive.description: References a previous task that provides the archive path (e.g., fileDialog or zip task).

destination.description: References a previous task that provides a destination folder path.

archive.description: For 'unzip' tasks, specifies the archive to extract. For 'zip' tasks, specifies the output archive path. Supports interpolation. Relative paths resolve against 'cwd' (default: the action's workspace folder). Unlike 'writeFile'/'appendFile', zip and unzip paths are NOT restricted to the workspace: they are meant to work on locations the user picks at runtime via fileDialog/folderDialog.

destination.description: For 'unzip' tasks, a string (supports interpolation) specifying the destination directory. Relative paths resolve against the action's workspace folder, and — like 'archive' — it is not restricted to the workspace.

source.description: File or directory paths to be compressed. Required for 'zip' type. Relative paths resolve against 'cwd' (default: the action's workspace folder); sources outside the workspace are allowed on purpose, since a folderDialog pick may live anywhere. Symlinks that resolve outside the selected source root are skipped and reported.

function.description: The function to apply for 'stringManipulation' type (stripExtension, basename, basenameWithoutExtension, dirname, extension, toLowerCase, toUpperCase, trim).

passTheResultToNextTask.description: Defaults to false. If true, the task output (stdout) is captured to be used as a variable in subsequent tasks (e.g., ${task.id.output}). If false or omitted, output is streamed live to the terminal and is not captured.

isOneShot.description: If true, the task is considered successful as soon as it starts. Useful for non-terminating processes like GUI applications. Only works when `passTheResultToNextTask` is false.

path.description: Destination path for 'writeFile' / 'appendFile' tasks. Supports variable interpolation. Relative paths resolve against the action's workspace folder and must stay inside it.

content.description: Content to write for 'writeFile' / 'appendFile' tasks. Supports variable interpolation.

encoding.description: File encoding for 'writeFile' / 'appendFile' tasks. Defaults to 'utf8'. 'utf8bom' prefixes a BOM (on appendFile, only when the target file does not already exist). 'ascii' replaces non-ASCII characters with '?'.

eol.description: Line-ending normalization for 'writeFile' / 'appendFile' tasks. Defaults to 'keep'.

overwrite.description: For 'writeFile': if false, the task fails when the target file already exists. Defaults to true. Ignored for 'appendFile'.

mkdirs.description: For 'writeFile' / 'appendFile': if true (default), missing parent directories are created automatically. If false, the task fails when the parent directory is missing.

allowSecretContent.description: Allows 'writeFile' / 'appendFile' / output.mode 'file' to persist content derived from sensitive runtime data such as password input, environment variables, clipboard text, or selected text. Without this flag such writes are refused. Files written under this flag are created with owner-only permissions (0600; no effect on Windows).

timeoutSeconds.description: Task-level timeout in seconds. If the task does not complete within this budget, it is canceled and the pipeline fails with a timeout error (subject to 'continueOnError'). 0 or omitted disables the timeout. Applies to every task type, including interactive ones.

continueOnError.description: If true, the pipeline continues to the next task when this task fails (including timeouts and user-canceled dialogs). The failing task's result becomes empty ({}). Defaults to false.

dependsOn.description: IDs of earlier tasks (within the same action) that must complete before this task. Combined with 'parallel' and auto-inferred dependencies from ${taskId.x} variable references to build the runtime task graph. TaskHub Doctor flags cycles, missing references, and self-dependencies.

parallel.description: If true, this task is exempt from the implicit 'wait for every preceding task in the array' barrier and may run concurrently with its siblings. It still waits for any task listed in 'dependsOn' and any task whose output it references via ${taskId.x} (auto-inferred). Note: 'parallel: true' is not fire-and-forget — a later task without 'parallel: true' is a sync barrier and waits for this task to finish. Interactive task types are flagged by TaskHub Doctor when 'parallel: true' because the runtime serializes their prompts via a UI mutex. Defaults to false.

when.description: Condition deciding whether this task runs. When false the task ends as skipped (not failed) and the action continues. References inside the condition are auto-inferred as dependencies, so the condition is evaluated after the task it looks at has finished. A task that plainly references a condition-skipped task is skipped too; use '${a.x ?? b.y}' when either branch's result is acceptable.

var.description: Value to compare, after variable interpolation. Usually a reference such as ${pick.value}.

equals.description: Run when the interpolated 'var' equals this string exactly.

notEquals.description: Run when the interpolated 'var' differs from this string.

matches.description: Run when the interpolated 'var' matches this regular expression (RegExp source, partial match).

in.description: Run when the interpolated 'var' equals one of these strings.

mode.description: Defines how to handle the task's output. Optional when only 'capture' is used.

language.description: Language mode for the editor tab when mode is 'editor'.

filePath.description: The path to save the output to when mode is 'file'. Can use variables.

content.description: The content to write to the file. Defaults to the task's stdout.

overwrite.description: If true, overwrite the target when mode is 'file'. Defaults to false. Can be a boolean or a string variable (e.g., '${someVar}') that evaluates to 'true'.

capture.description: Extract named variables from the task's string output. Each rule adds a `${task_id.<name>}` variable for downstream tasks. Only applies when the task returns a string output (shell/command with `passTheResultToNextTask: true`, or `stringManipulation`).

diagnostics.description: Scan the task's string output for compiler errors/warnings and surface them in the Problems panel. Same constraint as `capture` — requires a string-producing task (shell/command with `passTheResultToNextTask: true`, or `stringManipulation`). Use a preset shorthand like `"$gcc"` or define a custom `DiagnosticPattern`.

pattern.description: Regex pattern matched against each output line.

flags.description: Optional regex flags (e.g. 'i' for case-insensitive, 'm' for multiline). The `g` flag is silently stripped — the matcher iterates lines on its own.

file.description: 1-based capture group index for the file path. Relative paths resolve against the task's cwd.

line.description: 1-based capture group index for the (1-based) line number.

column.description: 1-based capture group index for the column number. Optional.

endLine.description: 1-based capture group index for the end-line number. Optional.

endColumn.description: 1-based capture group index for the end-column number. Optional.

severity.description: 1-based capture group index for severity text (error/warning/info/hint/note/fatal). Optional.

message.description: 1-based capture group index for the message text. Required.

defaultSeverity.description: Severity to use when the severity group is missing or unrecognized. Defaults to 'error'.

source.description: Label shown next to the message in the Problems panel. Defaults to 'taskhub'.

name.description: Variable name to expose as ${task_id.<name>}. Must be a valid identifier and must not shadow built-in keys (output, path, value, etc.).

regex.description: Regex pattern matched against the task output. If it matches, the specified capture group (default 1) is used.

group.description: Capture group index for `regex`. Defaults to 1. Use 0 to get the full match.

flags.description: Optional regex flags (e.g., 'm' for multiline, 'i' for case-insensitive).

line.description: Select one line by 0-based index. Negative values count from the end (-1 = last line). Ignored if `regex` is also provided.

trim.description: If true, apply trim() to the selected value.
